newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Food shares make gains on Nigerian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Food shares make gains on Nigerian bourse.

text.p: Food sector shares joined cement companies in making gains in active Thursday trading on the Nigerian stock exchange.
For technical reasons the all-share index could not be updated.
The biggest percentage rise was for Union Bank, one of Nigeria's big three, rising 20 kobo, or over three percent, to close at 6.40 naira. Other banks did not change.
In the food sector, Union Dicon Salt closed 50 kobo higher at 31.50 naira. Nigerian Bottling Co was 19 kobo up at 25.99 naira, while Flur Mills Nigeria rose 17 kobo to 11.50 naira.
Cement company shares also showed strongly.
West African Portland Cement gained 32 kobo to close at 27.57 naira. Cement Co of Northen Nigeria rose 12 kobo to 2.79 naira and Ashaka Cement was five kobo up at 14.70 naira.

Oil marketing company shares rose, but only a little. Unipetrol closed five kobo higher at 33.25 naira, Mobil, National Oil and Texaco were all three kobo up at 35.05 naira, 26.65 naira and 23.14 naira.
Guinness was down five kobo at 9.65 naira. Seven-Up Bottling Co was two kobo down at 2.15 naira, as was packaging firm CMB which finished at 4.60 naira. ($1=80 naira)
